prose.note: README.md must be able to state OpenTelemetry's and Coverlet's own floors, which are netstandard2.0 -- a true sentence naming a foreign framework. The allowance is scoped to ONE file and ONE version so the blast radius is a single document. Widening the rule instead would silently un-catch the bug it was written for.

expectations.note: A dark tool is a data point, not a failure. But a family in which NOTHING fires cannot distinguish 'correctly detected nothing' from 'the scan never ran', which is why the source-level tools below are the built-in negative control.

STATUS CHANGED AT THIS FAMILY. net45 and net46 sat below netstandard2.0, whose .NET Framework floor is net461, so Coverlet was excluded by the TARGET FRAMEWORK and exited 3. This family is above that floor: nothing about net462 excludes Coverlet. It is now held out only by NuGet being refused at this host's egress proxy, which is a setup gap -- exit 4. The 18 metrics it is primary for (statement 5, branch 7, delta 6) are dark for a completely different reason than they were one family ago, and collapsing 3 and 4 would hide that.

REPAIRED. unilyze is a real, actively maintained C# static analyzer (github.com/bigdra50/unilyze, MIT, v0.6.1) -- the "not a tool" finding was wrong. Whoever checked only searched PyPI (an unrelated Unicode-info package of the same name) and npm (404); the real tool is on NuGet (package `Unilyze`) and ships self-contained binaries on GitHub Releases, neither of which was checked. Verified by actually downloading and running v0.6.1 against this corpus's own domain code: it reports real per-method cyclomaticComplexity and cognitiveComplexity, and its peak findings match dataset.json's planted fixtures exactly (OrderKit.PricingService.PriceCents for cyclomatic, OrderKit.RiskScorer.Score for cognitive) on both this family and the net45 floor family. ``unilyze hotspot`` computes real git-churn x complexity via git log, a genuine alternative to pydriller for Code Churn. It is Class B -- its own Roslyn-based syntax walk needs no restore or build -- so the TFM is irrelevant to it, like Lizard/jscpd/Semgrep. Installed here from its GitHub Release binary, which this host's egress proxy does not block, unlike the NuGet-gated dotnet-tool channel every other analyzer here is stuck behind. It remains NOT a legitimate alternative for All Definition Coverage or All Uses Coverage (16 of the original 34 metrics): its own metric catalogue -- complexity, Halstead, cohesion, coupling, maintainability, churn -- has no def-use or data-flow analysis of any kind, so those 16 metrics are unaffected by this repair and stay exactly as broken as the roster defects doc already says -- see roslyn-dataflow.

toolData.whyNoProjectManifest: A .csproj, .sln, packages.config or lockfile inside a tool folder makes the platform treat that folder as its own project and run the whole roster against it. 19 folders x 312 branches. The TypeScript corpus hit this: 203 of 276 tasks in a run were fixture overhead.

languageMarker.note: The C# core of every fixture is C# 5-compatible so it is identical across all 13 families; the LanguageMarker class is what pins each file to this family's version.

semgrepRuleCorrection.problem: Semgrep does not interpolate metavariables inside a string literal, so the pattern required a string whose literal text is `SELECT $...ANY`. It matched nothing on any of the 312 branches, so the planted Flow 2 in InputSanitizer.BuildQuery was never measured. Nothing caught it because the runner grades on exit code and semgrep exits 0 at 4 findings or 5.
semgrepRuleCorrection.now: the format string is captured and tested with a metavariable-regex
